title: Atrial fibrillation: type, history and anticoagulation
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's atrial fibrillation and related long-term drug therapy.
note:
Chief Complaint: Routine follow-up for heart rhythm management.

HPI: The patient is a 68-year-old male presenting for a scheduled evaluation of his permanent atrial fibrillation. He reports feeling well and denies any palpitations, dizziness, or shortness of breath. He is currently managed on a rate-control regimen and reports consistent adherence to his medications. He has not experienced any falls or syncopal episodes since the last visit.

Medication List:
- Apixaban 5 mg twice daily
- Metoprolol 50 mg once daily

Exam: The patient is alert and oriented. He appears in no acute distress. Heart rate is 74 beats per minute, regular. Blood pressure is 122/78 mmHg. Lung sounds are clear to auscultation. No peripheral edema is noted.

Assessment: The patient has permanent AFib which is currently stable. He is maintaining an adequate heart rate on his current medication. He remains on apixaban for the prevention of systemic complications.

Plan: Continue current medications for rate control and anticoagulation. Follow up in six months for a repeat evaluation of his atrial fibrillation.

Electronically signed,
K. Nguyen, PA-C
May 14, 2026

distractors.why: Permanent has its own code; I48.20 is chronic AF, unspecified.
Apixaban, rivaroxaban, warfarin and similar drugs are anticoagulants (Z79.01).
